title: Design the deployed operation, not just the GraphQL shape
description: Choose an app workload, PostgreSQL model, and connector operation. The workbench traces whether the generated SDK contract is complete, bounded, and ownership-aware.

workloads.label: Browse product catalog
workloads.detail: Public summaries filtered by category, returned in small pages.

workloads.label: List my favorites
workloads.detail: A signed-in user reads only their saved product relationships.

workloads.label: Save one favorite
workloads.detail: Create an idempotent user-product relationship without trusting a client UID.

schemas.label: User, Product, Favorite
schemas.detail: Three normalized tables with a compound key on the join table.
schemas.invariant: The Favorite compound key prevents duplicate user-product pairs, while PostgreSQL foreign keys prevent references to missing users or products.

schemas.label: Favorites JSON on User
schemas.detail: One user row stores a client-shaped array of product snapshots.
schemas.invariant: A copied product snapshot can drift from the Product row and cannot rely on a relational foreign key for every embedded value.

schemas.label: Client-supplied owner ID
schemas.detail: The relationship is normalized, but the connector accepts an owner ID from the client.
schemas.invariant: Database constraints preserve row relationships, but they cannot prove that a client-supplied user ID belongs to the authenticated caller.

operations.label: ListCatalog
operations.detail: A public, paginated product summary operation with a category filter and a 24-row limit.
operations.auth: PUBLIC with an explicit public-data rationale

operations.label: ListMyFavorites
operations.detail: A USER operation that derives the owner filter from auth.uid and returns a bounded product projection.

operations.label: AddFavorite
operations.detail: A USER mutation that supplies userId from auth.uid and upserts the compound relationship.

operations.label: EverythingForProfile
operations.detail: A deeply nested USER query that returns broad user, product, and history projections without a useful page boundary.
